display.title: Reb Meir Refoels and the Agunah
display.summary_short: The Alter Rebbe sends an agunah to Vilna, to Reb Meir Refoels, the leading opponent of the Chassidim, who finds her missing husband among a wagon of prisoners.
display.summary_long: Reb Meir Refoels, head of the Vilna community and a fierce opponent of the Chassidim, became a devoted Chassid of the Alter Rebbe after witnessing two miracles; this is the first. After the song 'I Believe in Hashem', the storyteller explains what an agunah is: a woman whose husband has vanished, who cannot remarry. A Chassid brings his daughter, abandoned for three years, to the Alter Rebbe. After long thought, the Rebbe tells her to travel to Vilna and ask Reb Meir for help, and not to give up even if he calls it foolish. Reb Meir's wife sends her away, and Reb Meir himself has never heard of the man, but her tears move him to promise his help, and every morning she reminds him. Reb Meir often helps Jews arrested for living without a permit, and one day the chief of police shows him a list of prisoners passing through Vilna on the way to their punishment. One name is her husband's. She identifies him, and Reb Meir offers to free him if he gives her a get. Amazed at the Alter Rebbe's ruach hakodesh, Reb Meir begins to respect the Chassidim, though it takes a second miracle before he becomes one.
display.lesson: A tzaddik sees far beyond what others see; follow his instructions and do not give up.
